findings.title: Retry-count deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
findings.body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR only checks retryCount > 1, without method: SMS or scheduled: false. As written it can delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows that have retryCount > 1, and can delete an already-scheduled reminder, losing its referenceId so a Twilio message already scheduled can no longer be tracked or cancelled. The retry cleanup should be scoped to SMS (and unscheduled) reminders like the fetch below.

findings.title: Missing recipient or message never increments retryCount
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` when Twilio returns a falsy result, or in the catch block when an exception is thrown. If sendTo is missing/empty (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the generated message is empty, the block is skipped entirely: no scheduling attempt, no retryCount increment, and the row stays scheduled:false and is re-fetched on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That leaves one of the failure modes this PR is meant to bound retrying indefinitely; the empty-recipient/message case needs an increment or removal path too.

findings.title: Unhandled update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without any nested error handling. If that update fails — for example the reminder was deleted between findMany and the catch (Prisma P2025), or the original error was a database failure — the exception escapes the per-reminder loop, all remaining unscheduled reminders are never processed, and the handler returns an error instead of continuing. Previously the catch only logged and moved on. The increment should be wrapped so a failure to record the retry is logged without poisoning the rest of the batch.

findings.title: Retry increment uses a stale read instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both increments (here and in the catch block at line 195) write `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value fetched at the start of the run. The handler has no lock and makes slow sequential Twilio calls, so overlapping cron invocations can both read retryCount 0, both fail, and both write 1, losing increments and potentially keeping a permanently failing reminder below the >1 deletion threshold forever. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.
